Form schema is now a validated JsonSchema instead of a raw Map; Map-based construction stays available via the deprecated FormInputRequest.of(String, Map) and Builder.requestedSchema(Map) overloads, which route through JsonSchema.from(Map.class)/MapJsonFactory

Tachyon no longer starts tasks; TaskExecutionEngine dropped its generic start(), so a task-producing tool handler starts work itself and returns ToolResult.task(snapshot). Options for starting a task are the external engine's concern now.
Tasks facade no longer creates tasks; the application/workflow engine owns execution and hands Tachyon immutable TaskSnapshot projections via ToolResult.task(snapshot)

Cancellation is a cooperative request and the modern MCP response is an empty acknowledgement; callers observe eventual state through refresh instead of trusting a fabricated synchronous snapshot

TaskExecutionEngine (and the capability-flags registration it required) is replaced by TaskConnector.builder(), which is the single registration unit for the tasks capability; presence of each builder call is now the supported-operation signal, so there is no separate ServerFeature.Descriptor to bundle

Direct corollary of the TaskOptions removal above: Tachyon no longer starts tasks or invents their identifiers. A task-producing tool handler starts the external work and supplies its own stable taskId via ToolResult.task(snapshot), so no server-side generation strategy is needed

Not actually removed from the jar — annotated @ExperimentalApi for consistency with every other type in this package (TaskConnector, TaskSnapshot, the Task*Fn/Task*Request SPI), which Revapi's element filter excludes from the tracked stable surface. The whole Tasks feature is unreleased and still evolving; this closes the one inconsistency where TaskState/TaskSupport/Tasks were tracked as stable while their neighbors were not. (TaskState also dropped the unused canTransitionTo()/isActive() helpers as part of the same pass.)
